title: Hybrid retrieval
subtitle: Dense embeddings fused with BM25 and reranked, with every constant found by sweep.

stats.label: structure-aware chunks from about 19,000 files in one code index
configuration cells swept for the baseline's constants
embedding models in the bake-off before the sweep

lede: The memory service in FAFOHive serves agents that ask two kinds of question: an exact identifier such as a function name, and a description of behaviour in plain language. A dense vector search alone misses the first and lexical search alone misses the second, so I made code search and decision search hybrid. A query runs up to three streams at once (dense similarity on embeddings from a multilingual embedding model, weighted full-text search, and a metadata stream) and the ranked lists are fused with reciprocal-rank fusion. A classifier looks at each query first and sets how much each stream counts, because identifier queries and descriptive queries need different blends.
quote: I swept the baseline's constants, because a baseline tuned less carefully than the model it judges proves nothing.
evidence: Hybrid search and retrieval: dense, weighted full-text and metadata streams fused by reciprocal rank with cross-encoder rerank, over a code index of about 294,000 chunks.
Information retrieval evaluation: a hybrid baseline swept across 129 configuration cells that tied the model at recall at 10 (0.977) and beat it on long, buried requests, 0.90 to 0.67.
Search under load: bounded embedding and rerank endpoints, the reranker the first stage dropped under load with a flag, and a keyword-only mode with no embedding call.
author: Corey James
